1.why: The interface is static and clean, with no moving images, pop-ups, or other visible interruptions.

2.why: Headings, blue action buttons, highlighted progress steps, and green status messages make important items stand out clearly.

3.why: Each screen presents a prominent primary action and next-step reminder, although the Logs section adds some distraction.

4.why: The progress indicator, next-step banner, persistent logs, and one-step-at-a-time layout reduce how much the user must remember.

5.why: No visible password-manager control, autofill option, or remember-me feature appears in the screenshots.

6.why: Completed progress steps, persistent navigation, retained logs, and familiar labels help the user recognize previous items and actions.

7.why: The screens use short sentences, plain wording, large text, and clearly separated sections.

8.why: No error state or corrective error message is shown in any of the screenshots, so clear error guidance is not demonstrated.

9.why: Instructions explain what to enter, password requirements specify the required character types, and the Logs provide example practice codes.

10.why: Password and security-code actions are clearly labeled and presented sequentially, although no alternative such as face login is offered.

11.why: Most screens show only one primary task and one or two relevant actions at a time.

12.why: Green confirmations and next-step messages clearly report outcomes such as code preparation, password confirmation, reset completion, and privacy acceptance.

13.why: Every stage includes short task instructions, a next-step reminder, and an easily visible help-and-safe-sign-in section.

14.why: Input fields remain available and password recovery can be restarted, but no explicit retry control or recoverable mistake state is shown.

15.why: The same typography, colors, navigation, card layout, button styling, help section, and feedback patterns are used consistently throughout.
